profile.name: Prof. Dr. Srijan Lal Shrestha

profile.headline: Turning environmental and public-health data into evidence for Nepal.

bio: Prof. Dr. Srijan Lal Shrestha is Professor of Statistics and former Head of the Central Department of Statistics (CDS), Institute of Science and Technology, Tribhuvan University. He has taught and supervised MSc and PhD scholars in statistics at TU for more than two decades.

His research applies environmetrics, generalized linear models, time series and distributed lag methods to air pollution, climate-sensitive disease, drought and rainfall risk, and subnational human development in Nepal. He has collaborated with the WHO Urban Health Initiative and the Nepal Health Research Council.

He serves as Editor-in-Chief of the Nepalese Journal of Statistics and as a member of the IoST Ethical Review Committee. He received the NABIL Science and Technology Award (2016) and the Nepal Bidhya Bhushan "KA" (2009).

researchPillars.title: Environmetrics & Air Pollution Modeling
researchPillars.summary: PM2.5 and PM10 ambient and indoor air pollution modeling in Kathmandu Valley and rural Nepal, using curvilinear and gamma GLMs.

researchPillars.title: Environmental Burden of Disease & Epidemiology
researchPillars.summary: Distributed lag models for respiratory hospital admissions, mortality, childhood diarrheal disease and COVID-19 trends, with the WHO Urban Health Initiative and NHRC.

researchPillars.title: Climate Change & Hydrological Modeling
researchPillars.summary: Seasonally separated logistic and probabilistic drought and rainfall forecasting models over the Bagmati River Basin.

researchPillars.title: Socio-Economic & HDI Methodology
researchPillars.summary: Five-dimensional unequally weighted mapping and cluster analysis for subnational HDI assessment in Nepal, plus ecological footprint modeling.

researchPillars.title: Theoretical & Mathematical Statistics
researchPillars.summary: Censored negative exponential mixed distributions, nonparametric scatter plot smoothers, and categorical regression with optimal scaling.

supervision.intro: Prof. Shrestha supervises MSc and PhD research in Statistics at the Central Department of Statistics, IoST, Tribhuvan University. Prospective scholars with an interest in applied and environmental statistics are welcome to get in touch with a short research outline.
areas: Environmetrics and air quality modeling (PM2.5 / PM10)
Environmental epidemiology and burden of disease
Climate, drought and rainfall risk modeling
Time series and distributed lag models
Human development indices and socio-economic measurement
steps: Read two or three recent papers in the area you want to work on.
Prepare a one-page outline: question, data source and the methods you expect to use.
Send it through the contact form or by email, mentioning MSc or PhD.
